content: The case of the Hong Kong Alliance in Support of Patriotic and Democratic Movements of China (commonly known as the Alliance) on charges of inciting subversion of state power concluded with a verdict on Friday, August 21, after 24 days of trial. Lee Cheuk-yan and Chow Hang-tung, who denied the charges, ultimately heard the ruling. Former vice-chairperson Chow Hang-tung represented herself as a barrister in the case. Without access to a computer or internet in prison, she handwrote hundreds of pages of submissions. At her application, the court played footage from six consecutive years of the June 4 candlelight vigils, recreating the candlelight in Victoria Park, and broadcast testimony from eyewitnesses of the June 4 crackdown. In her opening submissions, Chow said with a smile: "I am the last defendant in this case, and also the last vice-chairperson of the Alliance — that is, the first defendant in this case... I am 41 years old this year, a barrister, with a simple background, nothing else." During her six days of testimony, she occasionally smiled and shed tears many times. What did the June 4 candlelight vigil and the slogan "End one-party dictatorship" mean to Chow Hang-tung? What was her "intent"? This episode of the Courtroom Watch programme continues to take readers into the courtroom, recreating Chow Hang-tung's testimony through voice enactment, as well as the judge's and prosecution's cross-examination. Recap: Voice enactment — Lee Cheuk-yan's testimony: There is no hatred in my heart, only love. Related coverage: The Alliance case.
